plan.title: 받은 장부도 적어주세요
plan.intent: The family demands loyalty while withholding even her meal. Jeonghui refuses the false debt and turns the demand for records into a documented handover, leaving the dinner on a sharp reversal.

facts.statement: Taeseop invokes family responsibility and Bokja agrees. Mansik asks them to talk after eating, although Jeonghui has no meal. She moves the pen back toward Taeseop.
Jeonghui will read the divorce agreement but refuses to sign the return-of-money statement because she did not take the money.
Taeseop demands all company records and keys by tomorrow morning. Records are ordered in the drawer, but Jeonghui does not open it.

Jeonghui proposes an inventory and a receipt for the records. Bokja objects to asking family for receipts. Jeonghui compares that request to their demand that she acknowledge an untrue eighty-million debt, and puts the earring record back in her pocket.

beats.action: Taeseop and Bokja invoke family responsibility to make Jeonghui accountable for company payments.
Mansik asks them to eat first while Jeonghui's missing bowl exposes the contradiction.
Jeonghui returns the pen and refuses the false debt statement, separating it from the divorce decision.
Taeseop demands keys and records, extending a hand toward Jeonghui while the document cabinet remains closed.
Jeonghui proposes an inventory and asks Taeseop to acknowledge the records he receives.
Bokja objects to receipts between family, and Jeonghui answers with the contradiction of the false debt acknowledgment.
Jeonghui returns the purchase record to her apron pocket and turns her attention to tomorrow's counted handover.

texts.speaker: c2
texts.text: 당신이 맡았으면 책임도 져야지. 좋을 때는 가족이고 불리하면 남이야?

texts.speaker: c1
texts.text: 이혼서류는 읽어보고 이야기할게요. 이 확인서에는 이름 못 써요.

texts.speaker: c2
texts.text: 그럼 장부 다 놓고 나가. 회사 열쇠도. 내일 아침까지 전부.

texts.speaker: c1
texts.text: 어떤 서류를 몇 권 넘겼는지요. 받으셨다고 적어주세요.

texts.speaker: c3
texts.text: 십 년 같이 산 식구한테 영수증을 받겠다는 거니?

texts.speaker: c1
texts.text: 제 돈 아닌 팔천만 원도 적으라고 하셨잖아요. 받은 장부 적는 건 어렵지 않으시겠죠.

texts.speaker: narrator
texts.text: 이제는 내일 넘길 종이가 몇 장인지부터 세어야 했다.

plan.staging: Keep the dinner room, outfits and five identities from the preceding page. Jeonghui is standing and has no meal setting. Mansik remains seated holding his spoon. The pen is moved toward Taeseop before the refusal; the document drawer remains closed and no key or ledger is handed over yet. The receipt is intact, returning to her apron pocket in the final moment. Taeseop's reaching hand is halted by the demand to acknowledge receipt. The divorce and money papers remain unsigned with abstract contents. End at the table tonight, before the next chapter's actual handover. All selected words are the original Korean dialogue or narration.
uncertainties: The exact drawer level is unspecified; the cabinet beside the table follows the room reference.
There is no physical inventory yet in this chapter, so the promise to make one is spoken, with no invented written list.

brief.style: European graphic-novel adult satire, bold ink contours, flat muted cream, charcoal and brick-red colors, believable middle-aged faces, expressive reactions, printed-paper texture.

moments.action: Taeseop faces standing Jeonghui with a forceful expression while seated Bokja nods in agreement.
Mansik sits over his rice bowl with his spoon, while Jeonghui stands at the table end beside a bare meal space.
Jeonghui faces Taeseop calmly, her hand beside the pen returned toward him on the table between the unsigned papers.
Taeseop extends his open hand toward Jeonghui, his expression demanding; the document cabinet beside the table remains closed.
Jeonghui and Taeseop face each other across the table, her calm proposal met by his puzzled expression.
Jeonghui holds Taeseop's gaze, keeping her hands beside the untouched papers as she sets the handover condition.
Bokja leans toward Jeonghui with an offended face and raised brows, her small gold hoops visible.
Jeonghui answers evenly beside the pen; Taeseop's outstretched hand rests halted on the dinner table.
Jeonghui slips the folded purchase record into her cream apron pocket, shoulders straight and face composed at the table end.

checks.name: sourceFidelity
checks.evidence: Seven beats preserve p55-76: family-responsibility pressure, meal contradiction, refusal with returned pen, tomorrow deadline, inventory proposal, family-receipt objection and reply, then receipt pocketing. Twelve selected texts are exact original lines; no written inventory or actual handover is invented.

checks.name: spatialFeasibility
checks.evidence: Five established adults remain at the same dinner. Mansik can speak with his spoon at his bowl; Jeonghui remains standing without a meal. Pen lies before Taeseop after being returned. Cabinet stays closed, hand reaches toward Jeonghui, and apron pocket accepts the existing receipt.

checks.name: temporalCausality
checks.evidence: Meal contradiction precedes refusal, then the records demand motivates the inventory requirement. Bokja's receipt objection precedes Jeonghui's reversal. The paper goes back in her pocket after Taeseop's hand stops; tomorrow's delivery remains future.

checks.name: visualLoad
checks.evidence: Nine panels give the longer debt refusal its own instant and the final retort its own instant. The short inventory question and answer split from the explanatory line; final caption accompanies only pocketing. No panel exceeds two text elements and there are no readable prop texts.

drawability.evidence: Nine single instants distinguish pressure, refusal, demand, condition and payoff. All actions fit the dining room and existing props. The final retort has its own reading space, and neither keys nor records have to materialize.

identity.evidence: Compared actual scene-three revision-two image: Jeonghui retains her sage blouse, apron, low bun and mole; Taeseop charcoal suit and combed black hair; Bokja short waves, burgundy and gold hoop. Mansik matches the cast and first-page seated elderly father in beige.

setting.evidence: The wooden table, adjoining beige kitchen, wooden cabinets, bowls and paper props persist. The bare meal space belongs to standing Jeonghui; the wider ending stays in the same dining room.

actionTransition.evidence: The receipt studied at the preceding ending precedes continued family pressure here and returns to her apron pocket at the end. The pen lies by Taeseop and the unsigned papers; tomorrow inventory remains only a spoken condition.

visualReview.evidence: Opened the actual nine-panel image and magnified panel 6 for inspection. Nine panels read in two, three, three and one across consecutive rows. Meal exclusion, unsigned-paper refusal, demanded records, family-receipt objection, retort and receipt pocketing are present. Speaker tails are correct. Eleven texts match, but text-9 starts with 이면 rather than 어떤, an actual lettering mismatch. The cabinet remains closed and there is no handover of records or keys. Some close views place Jeonghui at table height, but the wide opening and ending show her standing.

findings.evidence: Panel 6 text-9 visibly reads 이면 서류를 몇 권 넘겼는지요. 받으셨다고 적어주세요. The original starts 어떤 서류를. Preserve the exact first word 어떤 in a spacious legible balloon.
